slides.headline:
A boundary.
Not a barrier.
slides.message: The cell membrane regulates exchange between a cell and its surroundings.

slides.headline: Diffusion follows a concentration gradient.
slides.message: Net movement follows the gradient; individual particles continue to move in both directions.
steps: More particles leave the crowded side.

slides.headline: Not every molecule crosses the same way.
slides.message: Permeability depends on the molecule and the membrane.

columns.title: Simple diffusion
columns.body: Small nonpolar molecules can pass through the lipid bilayer.

columns.title: Facilitated diffusion
columns.body: Transport proteins help selected solutes move down their gradients.

slides.headline:
Against the gradient?
Energy is required.
slides.message: Active transport couples movement to an energy source. It is not simply faster diffusion.

slides.headline:
Ask what drives
the movement.
slides.message: Identify the solute, the membrane pathway and the direction of the concentration gradient.
